newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO and Russia to resume talks on May 6.
newsitem.headline: NATO and Russia to resume talks on May 6.

text.p: NATO and Russia are to hold a new round of talks in Luxembourg on May 6 in an attempt to strike a deal on a new post-Cold War pact between the two old enemies before the alliance proceeds with expansion eastwards.

NATO officials said on Monday Secretary-General Javier Solana and Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov would hold a fifth round of negotiations in the Grand Duchy to try to overcome remaining Russian objections.

Moscow has agreed 80 percent of a new document or charter giving it an upgraded relationship, including a permanent consultative mechanism with the alliance, but has tabled tough demands on military activities in new member states.

NATO says the limits on upgrading military facilities of countries set to join -- most probably Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic -- are unacceptable as they would give the new countries a "second-class" membership.
Last week, President Boris Yeltsin visited Germany and said he hoped the landmark NATO-Russia pact would be ready for signing in Paris on May 27.

That would clear the way for new members to be invited to join the alliance at a special summit in Madrid in July. The U.S. has reacted coolly to Yeltsin's comments, believing he is trying to coax the alliance into making some last-minute concessions.

NATO, stressing enlargement will go ahead whether the pact with Russia is finalised or not, says it cannot make deals over the heads of the new members, particularly anything which affects the sovereignty of a nation state.
At the same time, however, it has said it has "no intentions, no plans, no reasons" to place foreign troops or nuclear weapons on the territory of the new members.

Russia wants a commitment that it will never do so and says the new members must not be allowed to improve existing military facilities, such as airfield and even communication networks, to bring them in line with NATO requirements.
